messages.text: Woods given 'special opportunity' to design new course in Northern Ireland

metadata.summary: Tiger Woods has revealed he will design the first championship-standard links golf course built in Northern Ireland for more than 100 years, describing the project as a "special opportunity".
metadata.content: Tiger Woods: Former world No 1 hails 'special opportunity' to design new course in Northern Ireland with TGR Design | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Tiger Woods: Former world No 1 hails 'special opportunity' to design new course in Northern Ireland with TGR Design Bellarena will be TGR Design’s first course in Northern Ireland and the first new championship links to open in Northern Ireland in more than a century; TGR Design are a golf course design firm led by Tiger Woods Thursday 19 November 2026 16:41, UK Image: Tiger Woods has confirmed he will be involved in designing a new course in Northern Ireland Tiger Woods has revealed he will design the first championship-standard links golf course built in Northern Ireland for more than 100 years, describing the project as a "special opportunity". Reports linking the 15-time major champion with the proposed £30 million course at Bellarena on the north west coast between Limavady and Coleraine had been circulating for several weeks, ahead of Thursday's official announcement. Hospitality group Galgorm Collection is building the course, with construction set to get under way next year if the required planning approvals are secured. messages.text: WBC open door for Canelo to fight Hutchinson for light-heavy title

metadata.summary: The door is open for Canelo Alvarez to move back to light-heavyweight and challenge new world champion Willy Hutchinson.
metadata.content: WBC open door for Canelo Alvarez to challenge Britain's Willy Hutchinson for light-heavyweight world championship | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive WBC open door for Canelo Alvarez to challenge Britain's Willy Hutchinson for light-heavyweight world championship The WBC did not put in place a mandatory challenger for new light-heavyweight world champion Willy Hutchinson; that leaves the path open for Mexican superstar Canelo Alvarez to return to 175lbs and take on Hutchinson; Canelo returned from Terence Crawford defeat to reclaim WBC 168lbs title John Dennen Sports Journalist @johndennen Thursday 19 November 2026 13:18, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights as Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez shared a hard-fought world title clash with Christian Mbilli (Credit: DAZN) The door is open for Canelo Alvarez to move back to light-heavyweight and challenge new world champion Willy Hutchinson. Scotland's Hutchinson won his rematch with Joshua Buatsi on November 7 to secure the vacant WBC light-heavyweight title. Mexican superstar Alvarez reclaimed the WBC's super-middleweight belt when he outscored Christian Mbilli at the end of last month. Although 168lbs is his natural weight, Canelo has previous boxed at light-heavyweight, beating Sergey Kovalev but losing to Dmitry Bivol. messages.text: Nicholls breaks record for Jumps wins with Warwick triumph

metadata.summary: Paul Nicholls reflected on a “fantastic journey” after rewriting the record books by surpassing Martin Pipe’s all-time National Hunt tally for winners by a British trainer.
metadata.content: Paul Nicholls breaks record for National Hunt wins after surpassing Martin Pipe’s all-time tally with Warwick triumph | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Paul Nicholls breaks record for National Hunt wins after surpassing Martin Pipe’s all-time tally with Warwick triumph Ditcheat handler Paul Nicholls became the winning-most trainer in British National Hunt history, surpassing the great Martin Pipe's total of 3,390 when Knappers Hill crossed the line in front at Lingfield, donning the colours of Paul Barber Thursday 19 November 2026 14:19, UK Image: Paul Nicholls has trained more National Hunt winners than any other handler Paul Nicholls reflected on a “fantastic journey” after rewriting the record books by surpassing Martin Pipe’s all-time National Hunt tally for winners by a British trainer. The 14-time champion eclipsed Pipe's record of 3,930 wins at Warwick on Thursday after Knappers Hill toughed out victory in the Denis O'Connell Memorial Veterans' Handicap Chase under Sam Twiston-Davies, carrying the colours of the trainer's long-time friend and mentor Paul Barber. Nicholls, who has been training at Manor Farm Stables in Somerset since 1991 after first renting the yard from Barber, was thrilled to etch his name into the history of a sport in which he has long been a master of his craft. messages.text: Joseph retains place as England change nine for All Blacks and drop Pollock

metadata.summary: Will Joseph has retained his place on the wing for England's Nations Championship Test against New Zealand on Saturday, with Fin Smith among those restored and Henry Pollock dropped to the bench.
metadata.content: Nations Championship: Will Joseph retains England place vs New Zealand's All Blacks as Henry Pollock dropped amid nine changes | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nations Championship: Will Joseph retains England place vs New Zealand's All Blacks as Henry Pollock dropped amid nine changes Steve Borthwick makes nine changes to England XV for visit of All Blacks in Nations Championship on Saturday (2.10pm); Fin Smith, George Furbank, Tommy Freeman, Seb Atkinson, Jamie George, Fin Baxter, Joe Heyes, Ollie Chessum, Ben Curry all return; Will Joseph keeps place on wing Thursday 19 November 2026 14:00, UK Image: Will Joseph has retained his place in England's starting XV to face the All Blacks on Saturday Will Joseph has retained his place on the wing for England's Nations Championship Test against New Zealand on Saturday, with Fin Smith among those restored and Henry Pollock dropped to the bench. Joseph, who missed out on a place in England's matchday 23 for their 45-22 defeat of Australia a fortnight ago , started in last week's crushing 78-15 success over Japan, scoring five tries. The 24-year-old picked up just his second Test cap in that victory at Twickenham, and his first since July 2022 under Eddie Jones. He moves from right to left wing for the visit of the All Blacks. messages.text: Frick targets Premiership top-six for Aberdeen with 'heavy metal football'

metadata.summary: Aberdeen's new head coach Mario Frick will not just be happy with Scottish Premiership survival this season, insisting he wants a top-six finish.
metadata.content: Mario Frick: Aberdeen's new head coach targets Scottish Premiership top-six with 'heavy metal football' | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mario Frick: Aberdeen's new head coach targets Scottish Premiership top-six with 'heavy metal football' The 52-year-old has replaced Stephen Robinson at Pittodrie; the Dons are 11th in the Scottish Premiership; his first game in charge is at Kilmarnock on Saturday; watch Rangers vs Aberdeen on November 24, live on Sky Sports Alison Conroy Football Journalist @AlisonGConroy Thursday 19 November 2026 16:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New Aberdeen head coach Mario Frick reveals his top-six target after taking over at Pittodrie Aberdeen's new head coach Mario Frick will not just be happy with Scottish Premiership survival this season, insisting he wants a top-six finish. The 52-year-old takes over with the side sitting 11th in the table following Stephen Robinson's dismissal after their 4-0 defeat at Hibernian before the international break. Frick, who played 125 times for Liechtenstein, previously took charge of the national youth teams in his homeland before spells with Vaduz and Luzern, helping the latter to avoid relegation.
